title: Add policy compliance playbook, KMS circuit-breaker and differential audit sampler
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a documented compliance playbook for RBACv2 + audit handling
Introduce a KMS circuit-breaker that auto-fails over to alternate providers under high error-rate/latency
Add a differential audit sampler to increase audit capture for high-risk tenants and backfill redacted records
description: Context: Customers operating under strict regulatory regimes asked for two improvements after a recent post-mortem: (1) automated, opinionated guidance for oncall and SRE when KMS-related failures or residency warnings appear; (2) reduce missed audit signals during transient KMS failures while limiting storage costs. This PR delivers an operational 'policy compliance playbook' plus two runtime components: a KMS circuit-breaker and a differential audit sampler. Motivation: reduce incident toil and audit gaps while preserving data residency guarantees and minimizing spike in audit storage. Implementation summary: - Playbook: docs/compliance/playbooks/kms-residency-playbook.md with runbooks, escalation matrix, and example Linear templates for Paging and Postmortem. The playbook is vendor-agnostic and includes step-by-step commands for Dedicated and Private installs. - KMS circuit-breaker: runtime/kms/circuit_breaker.go adds a health-score based breaker that consumes KMS latency/error metrics and enforces per-tenant affinity windows. When the score crosses thresholds, requests are routed to configured fallback providers or to an offline-mode that returns explicit 5xx with an audit tag indicating redaction-required. Circuit-breaker supports operator-configured cooldown and jitter and exposes metrics: redwood_kms_breaker_state, redwood_kms_failover_rate, redwood_kms_last_signalled. - Differential audit sampler: observability/audit/sampler.go implements policy-based sampling where tenants marked as high-risk (by policy) get 100% audit capture during anomaly windows; low-risk tenants are sampled at a lower baseline. The sampler supports retrospective backfill: when an event is redacted due to KMS failure, a lightweight proof entry is retained and a backfill job (tools/audit/backfill_runner.py) attempts to reconcile once KMS returns. - RBACv2 policy templates: config/rbacv2/templates/compliance_templates.rego contains OPA snippets for enforcement points used by the sampler and breaker (e.g., allow_kms_failover_for_operator). - Tests and infra: Added unit tests for the breaker logic, integration test that simulates KMS latency spikes with a fake provider in perf-canary harness, and terraform changes to expose new alerts and SLOs in observability-pack. Checklist: - [x] Playbook drafted and reviewed by Security and SRE - [x] Breaker implemented with unit tests - [x] Sampler implemented and wired into audit pipeline - [x] Integration perf-canary scenario created - [x] Docs added and referenced in console runbook - [x] Linear tasks and alerts created (ENG-2145) Commits (top-level summaries): ["playbook: add initial kms residency and compliance playbook","runtime(kms): implement circuit-breaker with health scoring","observability: add metrics and dashboards for kms breaker","audit: implement differential sampler and backfill proof entries","rbacv2: add OPA templates for failover and sampler decisions","tests: add unit + perf-canary integration tests","infra: expose breaker alerts and create PagerDuty escalation policy","docs: link playbook from onboarding guide"] Changed files (high-level): ["docs/compliance/playbooks/kms-residency-playbook.md","runtime/kms/circuit_breaker.go","runtime/kms/circuit_breaker_test.go","observability/metrics/dashboards/kms-breaker.json","observability/audit/sampler.go","tools/audit/backfill_runner.py","config/rbacv2/templates/compliance_templates.rego","perf-canary/scenarios/kms-failure-spike.yaml","terraform/observability/alerts/kms_breaker.tf","console/runbooks/kms-failover.md"] Review conversation (high-level entries): ["Ibrahim Khan: Can the breaker be tenant-scoped so a noisy tenant doesn't impact others? Response: yes, breaker uses per-tenant windows and a global fallback flag; implementation note added.","Sofie Alvarez: Please ensure the backfill proof entries are safe to store without leaking PII — suggested a redact-only hash form. Response: sampler retains only a CRC+timestamp+policy-id; code updated to avoid message bodies in proofs.","Rachel O'Neill: Add an integration test that simulates provider rotation during an ongoing flow. Response: Added perf-canary scenario and CI run step.","Security review (J. Patel): Approve after small rego policy change to deny automatic failover for tenants with strict data-residency attribute. Response: Updated compliance_templates.rego to include residency-allowlist check.","SRE review: Request to expose breaker state on the /healthz endpoint for easier runbook checks. Response: Exported breaker state and added a cached health endpoint with 1s TTL."] CI summary: "All CI checks passed on merge: unit tests (go, python) passed, linter fixed, perf-canary integration scenario ran in the CI cluster and flagged minor timing flakiness that was addressed by adding retry backoff. E2E job completed against an internal staging env with a fake KMS provider. No policy violations found by the rbac linter." Risk and mitigation: "Risk: Improper failover could violate residency constraints. Mitigation: RBACv2/OPA denylist prevents failover for tenants with residency constraints; PR contains an emergency kill-switch boolean operator flag and automated audits that alert on any route-to-fallback events. Risk: audit storage blowup. Mitigation: differential sampling caps baseline sampling for low-risk tenants and only escalates during anomaly windows; backfill proof entries are compact and do not contain full payloads." Deployment plan: "Staged rollout: enable breaker in shadow mode for 72h (metrics only), then enable per-tenant targeted rollouts behind a feature flag environment variable, then global opt-in after 2 week observation. Playbook linked for oncall. Merge method: squash and merge. Merged by: Sohail Mehta on 2026-02-03." Additional notes: "This PR intentionally keeps the playbook vendor neutral and includes explicit command snippets for both Dedicated and Private installer workflows. Follow-on work: metrics-driven auto-tuning of breaker thresholds (ENG-2201).
